latest_nl_proof:
Fix integers m and g with m >= 2 and g >= 0, and let K_{m,g} be as in the statement.

We prove that K_{m,g} is finite.

Take any k = (k_1,\dots,k_{m-1}) in K_{m,g}. By definition, each k_r is a positive integer, so for every r \in \{1,\dots,m-1\} we have k_r >= 1. Also, again by definition,

k_1 + \cdots + k_{m-1} = g.

Therefore every element of K_{m,g} is, in particular, a positive integer (m-1)-tuple whose coordinates sum to g.

So we have the inclusion

K_{m,g} \subseteq S_{m,g},

where

S_{m,g} := \{(a_1,\dots,a_{m-1}) \in \mathbf Z_{>0}^{m-1} : a_1+\cdots+a_{m-1}=g\}.

The additional inequalities appearing in the definition of K_{m,g} only further restrict this set, so it is enough to show that S_{m,g} is finite.

For each r = 1,\dots,m-1 and each (a_1,\dots,a_{m-1}) \in S_{m,g}, since the coordinates are positive and sum to g, we have

1 <= a_r <= g.

Hence every element of S_{m,g} lies in the finite Cartesian product

\{1,2,\dots,g\}^{m-1}

when g >= 1. Since a finite Cartesian product of finite sets is finite, S_{m,g} is finite.

If g = 0, then S_{m,g} is empty, because no positive integers can sum to 0; thus S_{m,g} is finite in this case as well.

Since K_{m,g} \subseteq S_{m,g} and S_{m,g} is finite, K_{m,g} is finite.

This proves the lemma.
role_in_parent: Supplies finiteness of each coordinate layer, needed to turn an injection into a cardinality inequality.
statement_nl: Fix integers m and g with m >= 2 and g >= 0. Define K_{m,g} to be the set of all tuples k = (k_1, ..., k_{m-1}) of positive integers such that: for all integers i and j with 1 <= i <= j <= m-1, if i + j < m then k_i + k_j >= k_{i+j}, if i + j > m then k_i + k_j + 1 >= k_{i+j-m}, and also k_1 + ... + k_{m-1} = g. Then K_{m,g} is a finite set.

domain_restrictions: m is an integer with m >= 2
g is an integer with g >= 0
k is a (m-1)-tuple of positive integers: for each r in {1,...,m-1}, k_r ∈ Z_{>0}
Index constraints in the universal clause: 1 <= i <= j <= m-1

Inequalities are applied only when i+j < m or when i+j > m; the expression k_{i+j} requires i+j in {1,...,m-1} (consistent with i+j<m), and the expression k_{i+j-m} requires i+j-m in {1,...,m-1} (consistent with i+j>m)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every fixed integers m,g with m>=2 and g>=0, the set K_{m,g} := { k ∈ Z_{>0}^{m-1} : (∀ i,j integers with 1<=i<=j<=m-1) [ (i+j<m => k_i+k_j>=k_{i+j}) ∧ (i+j>m => k_i+k_j+1>=k_{i+j-m}) ] ∧ (k_1+...+k_{m-1}=g ) } is finite.
